newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BANK OF NEW ZEALAND LAUNCHES HIRE PURCHASE CARD.
newsitem.headline: BANK OF NEW ZEALAND LAUNCHES HIRE PURCHASE CARD.

text.p: The Bank of New Zealand on Thursday launched a new credit card designed to make it easier to buy on hire purchase or obtain a personal loan, the New Zealand Press Association reported.
The card, called Activator, will have an interest rate of 13.75 percent, about a third less than most credit card rates.
It is the first of its type offered by a large trading bank. Activator can be used to buy large consumer items like furniture, whiteware appliances or to do home renovations.
The BNZ is owned by the National Australia Bank.

National Mutual relaunched its Freedom card this year. It allows customers to borrow up to $20,000 to purchase anything they want. An interest rate of 16 percent is charged, but there are no other costs.

Brent McKenzie, chief manager of cards at the BNZ, said the Activator's current interest rate compared well with an average of 16 percent for personal loans, 20 percent for credit cards and between 20 percent and 30 percent for hire purchase.
The card attracts a $20 fee but only in the month when a purchase is made. Monthly repayments are five percent of the outstanding amount or $50, whichever is greater.
McKenzie said New Zealanders spent NZ$800 million last year on hire purchase and about $1 billion on personal loans. The card was expected to make significant inroads in those markets.
Activator could also be used at automatic teller machines to withdraw cash.
McKenzie said the card was aimed at non-BNZ customers as well as its own customers.

"Activator places the power in the hands of the consumer. For decades, hire purchase and personal loans have dominated the finance market for larger items. Now there is a means for consumers to obtain finance for larger items as and when needed,
and at considerably lower interest rates," he said.
The credit limit depends on each individual's circumstances.
